standard.title: Algorithms with addition and multiplication
standard.description: Follow and create algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that use addition or multiplication to generate sets of numbers; identify and describe any emerging patterns
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can follow and create algorithms to investigate numbers and describe emerging patterns (AC9M3N07). They have not yet used multiplication as the operation in an algorithm or represented algorithms as formal flowcharts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students follow and create algorithms using addition or multiplication to generate number sequences, represent these as flowcharts, and identify and describe emerging patterns.

nodes.label: Follow a step-sequence algorithm
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can follow a given algorithm using addition or multiplication to generate a number sequence.
nodes.minimum_width: Follow a written algorithm (list of steps) using multiplication by a constant to generate at least 5 terms of a sequence; identify one pattern in the sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Follow algorithms using both addition and multiplication to generate sequences; record results systematically; identify and describe emerging patterns including recognising that sequences can be extended indefinitely.
wider: Compare sequences generated by an additive algorithm (start at 1, add 3 each time) and a multiplicative algorithm (start at 1, multiply by 3 each time) — contrasting linear vs exponential growth visually
Use a calculator to follow algorithms and extend sequences, verifying patterns across many terms
success_criteria: Students can correctly follow a multi-step algorithm to generate the next several terms of a sequence
Students can identify and describe at least one pattern in the generated sequence

nodes.label: Represent algorithms as flowcharts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can represent an algorithm as a flowchart using standard symbols for steps and decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Represent one algorithm as a basic flowchart with at least one step and one decision node; explain what each symbol represents.
nodes.typical_width: Create flowcharts representing multiplication-based algorithms; use the flowchart to trace and verify sequence generation; explain how the decision node determines when to stop the sequence.
wider: Represent the same algorithm in two forms (written steps and flowchart) and compare — discussing which is clearer for different purposes
Design a flowchart that generates multiples of a given number and test it with classmates — debugging the flowchart where the output is incorrect

response_modes.reason: Flowcharts require students to decompose an algorithm into explicit sequential and conditional steps. The reasoning scaffold — 'what happens at each step, and what decision is being made?' — must be made explicit before students can create their own flowcharts accurately.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot decompose an algorithm into sequential and conditional steps cannot meaningfully create their own algorithms in Node 3 — creation requires the same decomposition skill that following and representing flowcharts develops.
success_criteria: Students can create a basic flowchart representing an addition or multiplication algorithm
Students can trace a flowchart to generate the first several terms of a sequence

nodes.label: Create algorithms and identify patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an algorithm using addition or multiplication and identify patterns in the generated sequence.
nodes.minimum_width: Create one algorithm (specifying starting value and operation) to generate a number sequence; identify and describe an emerging pattern.
nodes.typical_width: Create multiplication and addition algorithms; use digital tools (spreadsheets) to generate long sequences; identify patterns including multiples, geometric growth, and patterns in the ones digit; describe patterns in words and explain how the algorithm produces them.
wider: Use a spreadsheet with a 'fill down' formula to generate 100 terms and investigate patterns that only become apparent over many terms (e.g. repeating units digits in multiples)
Create and compare algorithms that produce the same sequence through different rules, investigating whether the same pattern can have different generating algorithms
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Algorithm creation connects mathematical computation to computational thinking. Students who design and test algorithms develop systematic thinking habits that transfer across contexts. The spreadsheet extension makes patterns visible at scales impossible to see by hand.
success_criteria: Students can design an algorithm that generates a specified type of sequence (e.g. multiples of 4)
Students can identify and describe a pattern in a sequence they have generated and explain how the algorithm produces it
